conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim is false, citing physiological studies and fact-checking consensus showing that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks does not cause dangerous carbon-dioxide buildup.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
Your skepticism is well-supported by the evidence: the claim that prolonged cloth or surgical mask use causes dangerous CO2 buildup is false, or at best highly overstated.

**What the research shows:** A key study on gas exchange in healthy people and COPD patients found no significant differences in oxygen or CO2 levels with or without a surgical mask—even in people with severely damaged lungs (https://www.foxnews.com/health/face-masks-dont-cause-carbon-dioxide-build-up-or-restrict-breathing). Direct air-sampling measurements found CO2 concentrations near the face while masked were comparable to normal environmental fluctuations (500–2200 ppm)—far below levels considered hazardous (https://aaqr.org/articles/aaqr-20-07-covid-0403.pdf). A more recent systematic review and meta-analysis of N95 and surgical masks found that while N95s raised local CO2 slightly more than surgical masks during exertion, there was "no big difference" overall compared to no mask, and the effect sizes seen were not clinically meaningful (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11386028/).

**Fact-checking consensus:** Multiple independent fact-checkers (AFP, USA Today, Reuters, AP, Poynter/IFCN affiliates) reviewed the same viral claims and rated them false or misleading, citing medical experts who note that masks are gas-permeable and cannot meaningfully trap CO2 to cause hypercapnia (https://factcheck.afp.com/prolonged-use-face-masks-unlikely-cause-hypercapnia).

**Caveat:** One small pilot study using photoacoustic spectroscopy reported elevated CO2 and ethylene near the mask surface and called for further research, but this was not a clinical/physiological measurement of blood gases and doesn't override the broader evidence base.

**Conclusion:** The weight of physiological evidence and fact-checking consensus confirms the claim is false.
